digest.component_or_area: Test reliability oracles (subprocess and network timeouts)
propositions: Test-only real-time windows in snapshot fetch stall abort and ACLI subprocess timeout tests consume multi-second wall time (15s and 9s respectively) while test contracts concern throughput, retry schedule, and process cleanup rather than elapsed seconds.

Snapshot stall-abort test serves a real loopback remote for 15 seconds to verify sustained bytes above configured floor survive one complete low-speed window; a 1-second injected window with real traffic above floor for >1 window duration preserves the semantic contract at reduced latency.

ACLI subprocess read-retry test uses 1-second call timeout plus real production backoff sleeps (2s/4s schedule) across three child processes; sub-second injected timeouts with logical backoff recording (no sleeping) and real process spawning preserve the retry schedule and process cleanup contract.
Production timeout, stall, grace, drain, attempt, and backoff defaults must remain unchanged (byte-for-byte) in all cases.

Both focused test modules must pass with both target tests completing in low single-digit seconds without absolute upper-bound pass assertions, brittle wall-clock thresholds, or runner/skip/xfail changes.
